overview: Both are tough connective tissue bands, but they connect different structures — tendons link muscle to bone, ligaments link bone to bone.
genZNote: Tendon: the rope connecting muscle to bone. Ligament: the rope connecting bone to bone at a joint.

aspects.label: What It Connects
aspects.valueB: Connects bone to bone at a joint.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Transmits the force of muscle contraction to move a bone.
aspects.valueB: Stabilises joints and limits excessive movement, preventing dislocation.

aspects.label: Elasticity
aspects.valueA: Relatively inelastic, built to transmit force efficiently.
aspects.valueB: Slightly more elastic than tendons, allowing a small range of flexible movement.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Achilles tendon, connecting the calf muscle to the heel bone.
aspects.valueB: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), stabilising the knee joint.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A torn ACL (a ligament injury) versus a torn Achilles tendon (a tendon injury) are both extremely common exam and real-world examples for this exact distinction.
overlay.memoryTrick: Tendon = 'T' for muscle-To-bone. Ligament = bone-to-bone, stabilising joints ('L' for Linking bones).
overlay.commonMisconception: Tendons and ligaments are not made of the same tissue doing the same job — both are dense connective tissue, but their composition and elasticity are tuned differently for their specific roles.
